methodological_rigor.justification: This is a reasonably strong retrospective prediction-model study: the authors use patient-level splitting into training, validation, and held-out test sets, keep all images from a patient in one split, and add ablation analyses in the Results section. The main weakness is that it remains a single-institution design with no external or prospective validation, which the Discussion explicitly notes. The statistical work is appropriate for the question, with ROC/AUC comparisons, DeLong testing, and Bonferroni-adjusted morphology comparisons, but it stops short of external calibration or transportability assessment.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript is a retrospective, single-center prediction study using bone marrow smears and matched FISH labels, which fits a low-level cohort-style evidence category rather than an interventional design. Its clinical relevance is plausible because it targets cytogenetic risk stratification in multiple myeloma and frames the model as a rapid screening tool for FISH triage and resource-limited settings, but those uses are not prospectively demonstrated. The translational path is real, but it remains unvalidated.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the closest fit because the work develops and internally evaluates a prediction model from patient-level labels. The manuscript reports the cohort, preprocessing, segmentation, model architecture, internal test performance, and several ablations, but it does not include protocol registration, an external validation cohort, or any explicit data/code repository. No public data or code sharing is stated, so reproducibility is limited to the prose methods.

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is methodological and empirical: the paper combines a hematology-specific foundation model, StarDist-based cell extraction, and attention-based MIL to predict multiple myeloma cytogenetic markers from Wright-Giemsa smears. That is a meaningful extension beyond the prior MM morphology papers and the AML/MDS work cited in the Introduction, even though the manuscript itself acknowledges related prior studies on bone marrow aspirates and H&E biopsies. The novelty is strong but not field-defining because it is still a single-center retrospective validation.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is organized clearly and the abstract tracks the body of the manuscript, with informative figures and tables that support the narrative. At the same time, the prose is repetitive in places, contains several awkward or overextended sentences, and repeatedly overstates clinical readiness relative to the retrospective evidence base. Overall it is readable and structured, but not yet polished enough to merit a top writing score.

key_strengths: Strong single-cell computational pipeline with patient-level splitting, internal test performance, and ablation analyses.
Clear translational target in MM cytogenetic risk stratification, with attention maps tied back to known morphology-genetics associations.
The manuscript is well structured and the figures/tables are aligned with the main claims.
key_concerns: Single-institution retrospective design with no external or prospective validation limits generalizability.
No public data or code release is stated, so reproducibility is incomplete.
Several clinical deployment claims go beyond what the internal validation data can support.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid translational AI paper with credible internal validation and clear biological motivation, but it is still constrained by single-center retrospective evidence. That makes tier 3 the plausible ceiling, with minor revisions centered on tightening claims and clarifying reproducibility.
